meta.title: Primordial Paradox music recipes, scope fox (soundfont era RPG score technique, described from public analysis)
meta.citation_note: Every recipe cites source ids from knowledge/music-styles/fox.md section 15. Full titles, URLs and read dates live there, not here, because this directory is scanned by the project's clean-room gate.
meta.chip: NES 2A03 (2 pulse, triangle, noise, DPCM) plus optional VRC6 (2 pulse, saw). Fox's own scores are soundfont and sample based; these recipes translate the technique, they do not reproduce the palette

conventions.frames: one frame is 1/60 s (16.7 ms) on NTSC; at 124.5 bpm a beat is 29 frames and a sixteenth 7 frames
conventions.beats_per_note_target: 0.42 to 1.12, measured in the Fox reference set
conventions.chord_complexity_band: 11 to 59 on a scale where 50 is average

recipes.name: One cell, many dresses transformation ladder
recipes.when_to_use: Whole score planning. One cell per character, transformed rather than rewritten, in the order listed here.

params.ladder: statement; rhythm variation; inversion; augmentation; mode swap on the accompaniment only; fragment extraction; instrumentation swap; tempo remap
params.never_change: interval vector shape and first three note contour

forbidden: rewriting the interval vector to fit a new chord
stating the cell in full in every cue that uses it
applying two operations in the same statement

recipes.name: Fragment extraction from a parent cell
recipes.when_to_use: Creating a second or third theme that must feel related to a character cell without restating it.

params.rhythm_change_factor: at least 2x against the parent rhythm
params.register: same octave band as the parent
params.assignment: new meaning, carried in the cue the listener hears third

forbidden: a window that spans more than half the parent cell
reusing the parent rhythm unchanged
more than two derived cells from one parent

recipes.name: Re-bar the cell instead of changing metre
recipes.when_to_use: A cue that needs to feel like a different time signature while the grid and the loop stay simple.

params.operation: give the long first note a whole 3/4 bar, or start the cell on the and of 1 in 4/4

forbidden: changing the notes at the same time as the accents
meter changes at section boundaries with no scene reason
a 7/8 or 5/4 bar presented as a Fox device

recipes.name: Whole-track detune, 25 to 40 cents
recipes.when_to_use: A cue that must sound slightly wrong or slightly elsewhere: a memory, a distortion, a false room.

params.applies_to: every pitched channel of the cue, cue level decision
params.documented_cases: 25 cents above C sharp major, 40 cents above A minor

forbidden: per note detune used as vibrato
detune above 50 cents, which reads as a wrong key, not a colour
detuning the bass only

recipes.name: Fifteen percent speed memory cue
recipes.when_to_use: A flashback, a dream, or a location the player has already left.

params.source_material: an existing cue in the same cell family
params.decay: fast, music box or piano per FOX-20

forbidden: using the stretched cue as a boss or battle cue
adding a drum kit
more than two voices
pitch shifting as well as stretching

recipes.name: Retrograde a finished cue
recipes.when_to_use: A false victory, a bad route, or a track that must feel like the same music with the meaning inverted.

params.operation: time reverse the melodic voices only
params.documented_case: a final boss cue that is the hopeful cue reversed
params.loudness: match the source cue within 1 dB

forbidden: reversing the drum kit, which produces pre-echo artefacts
reversing and transposing in the same cue
using retrograde as the only change in a cue the player hears twice

recipes.name: Medley coda over a 4 bar grid
recipes.when_to_use: A finale or credits cue that must pay off every character cell in the score.

params.sections: one cell family per section, 4, 8 or 12 bars each
params.section_order: the order the cells were introduced in the story
params.one_shared_engine: the same rhythm section under every section
params.documented_reference: four cells across 3:01 with section starts near bars 31, 48, 56, 63, 80 and 95 at 171 bpm

forbidden: changing the drum feel between sections
a new cell introduced in the coda
quoting all four of our cells in full in any other cue

recipes.name: Suspended dominant as the default
recipes.when_to_use: Every cue. The dominant in this style is a sus chord that resolves late or not at all.

params.resolution: at the next bar, or omit and let the tonic arrive directly
params.measured_share: sus4 plus sus2 is 0.207 of chord beats in the reference corpus
params.voicing: root and fifth on the two pulses, fourth on the second pulse at the octave

forbidden: a plain major dominant triad as the resting chord
resolving the fourth upward on the same beat it sounds
sus4 on the final chord of a cue

recipes.name: Flat six shadow bar
recipes.when_to_use: Two to four bars in a sad or approaching-threat cue, where the tonic should feel borrowed from elsewhere.

params.chord: bVI major, or bVI in first inversion
params.measured_share: bVI is 0.034 of chord singles, bVI6 0.027
params.melody: hold a note of the tonic triad across the change so the third of bVI clashes by a semitone
params.return: to i through the dominant or directly

forbidden: two consecutive bVI bars with the same voicing
using bVI as the cadence chord
combining with a tritone pivot in the same four bars

recipes.name: Neapolitan sus4 two bar shadow
recipes.when_to_use: Dread, dungeon and boss approach cues, where the tonic should sound watched.

params.measured_share: 0.026 of chord singles, the fourth largest single label behind i, i7 and Vsus4
params.voicing: flat second in the bass, fourth and flat seventh above
params.melody: oscillate on the fifth above the tonic, which stays consonant over bIIsus4
params.placement: one statement per 16 bar section, never the last two bars

forbidden: resolving bIIsus4 to the tonic without a dominant in between
more than one statement per 16 bars
using it under a melody that also moves chromatically

recipes.name: Chromatic slip pivot with a held melody note
recipes.when_to_use: One moment per boss cue, where the fight turns or the character drops the mask.

params.pivot: tonic minor triad to the diminished triad a semitone above
params.melody: hold a note that becomes a tritone against the new chord
params.resolution: back to the tonic, or to the subdominant, within 2 bars
params.documented_bar: bar 10 of a 144 bpm boss cue
params.voicing: the diminished chord on the second pulse, root and the conflicting note on the first

forbidden: holding the pivot for a whole section
two pivots in the same 8 bars
resolving the tritone immediately, which removes the effect

recipes.name: Augmented sixth substitution
recipes.when_to_use: The climax bar of a boss cue, one statement only.

params.chord: loose augmented sixth: flat sixth degree, tonic, raised fourth, and the dominant in the bass
params.duration: 1 chord, half a bar to a bar
params.resolution: the tonic in first inversion, or the dominant
params.documented_bar: bar 40 of a 144 bpm boss cue

forbidden: more than one per cue
placing it before the hook's first statement
using it in a town or field cue

recipes.name: Diatonic melody over a chromatic bass
recipes.when_to_use: Battle and boss cues where the melody must stay singable while the floor moves.

params.bass_chromatic_share: up to 0.25 of bass notes outside the key
params.bass_motion: half step approach into each chord root
params.chord_bass_melody: keep the counter line within 12 semitones of the melody motion, aim high on that metric

forbidden: chromatic melody and chromatic bass at the same time
bass approach notes on a strong beat of the hook
chord tone share above 0.75, which removes the Fox lean

recipes.name: Repeated note pedal hook
recipes.when_to_use: Battle, boss and field hooks that must be recognisable from rhythm alone.

params.measured_reference: 0.237 of intervals in the reference corpus are unison, and the top two interval patterns are 0 0 and 0 0 0
params.duration_cell: one sixteenth per attack at battle tempo
params.movement_after: one leap of a fourth or larger, then step back

forbidden: more than 6 repeats without a change of pitch or timbre
repeating on the tonic only, which flattens the hook
a repeated note with no rhythmic variation on the second statement

recipes.name: Narrow chorus, wide verse
recipes.when_to_use: Title, boss and finale cues with a singable core and a busy accompaniment.

params.wide_material: arpeggios and register jumps in the sections where the harmony is static
params.narrow_material: the hook itself, one voice, no doubling

forbidden: the hook living in the wide section
range above 12 semitones on the hook
doubling the hook in the wide section, which hides the narrowing

recipes.name: Two bar hook with an 8 to 16 bar drop
recipes.when_to_use: Boss cues. Thin texture first, full texture at the drop.

params.pre_drop_instrumentation: one lead and one percussion element, or lead only
params.drop_marker: one bar fill and a one beat silence before the drop

forbidden: an intro longer than 16 bars without a new idea
the hook first appearing after the drop
two drops in the same loop

recipes.name: Ostinato boss engine plus one interval cell
recipes.when_to_use: Boss themes that must be memorable from the first loop without a long melody.

params.harmony: flat seven as the most used chord, or i to bVII as the two chord engine
params.cell: 3 to 5 notes, one leap, repeated per bar
params.drum: four on the floor or a rock backbeat, fills every 4 bars
params.bass: eighth pulse with an octave jump at the section change

forbidden: a tempo below 140 in a boss cue
the cell changing every bar
more than four chords in the loop

recipes.name: Tempo ladder per cue type
recipes.when_to_use: Whole score planning, to stop every cue landing on the corpus median.

params.measured_corpus: median 124.5, mean 145.3, min 100, max 240, 43 percent in 120 to 139
params.rule: no more than one third of the score inside a single 20 bpm band

forbidden: using 124.5 as the default for every cue
a boss cue under 140
two adjacent cues within 4 bpm of each other in different cue types

recipes.name: Serious idiom comedy cue, 15 to 40 seconds
recipes.when_to_use: Joke encounters and absurd characters.

params.idiom: polka, march, waltz or fanfare played completely straight
params.wrong_instrument: exactly one instrument that does not belong
params.harmony: functional, no jokes in the chords
params.measured_reference: comedy tracks in the reference OST run 0:17 to 0:57 while set pieces run 2:30 to 4:44

forbidden: a comedy cue longer than 60 s
comedy in the harmony as well as the timbre
two wrong instruments, which reads as noise rather than a joke

recipes.name: Two voice restraint cue
recipes.when_to_use: Memory, death, home and sleep scenes. The default answer when a section feels weak.

params.palette: pulse 0.125 with fast decay plus pulse 0.25 with 16 step decay, or pulse plus triangle
params.noise: none, or one hit per 8 bars
params.cell: the character cell in full, once per 8 bars
params.dynamics: keep 10 to 12 dB below the full band version of the same cue

forbidden: arpeggiated chords in a restraint cue
a drum kit
adding a third voice to fix a weak bar instead of removing one

recipes.name: Fragment quote on the second pulse
recipes.when_to_use: Any cue that quotes another character's cell without stating it in full.

params.quote_voice: pulse 2, or VRC6 pulse 3 when the lead is busy
params.octave: same as the parent, or one octave below
params.duration: one bar, at a section boundary or under a held chord
params.rhythm: changed by at least 2x from the parent

forbidden: quoting on the lead voice while the cue's own cell is stated
two different quotes in the same bar
quoting the first three notes of the parent cell, which is the recognisable head and reads as a reprise rather than a hint

recipes.name: Arrangement changes before the melody
recipes.when_to_use: Every re-use of a location or character cell. The rule that keeps a small score from sounding repetitive.

params.order_of_change: instrumentation, then register, then tempo, then metre, then mode, and the melody last
params.min_changes_per_reuse: two of duty, decay, octave, voice count
params.melody_change: only when the story changes the character's meaning
params.documented_model: the same melody as solo guitar, then piano and strings, then a music box

forbidden: changing the melody and the instrumentation in the same statement
reusing a cell with only a volume change
adding a voice on a reuse

recipes.name: Polka one-two with a driving kit
recipes.when_to_use: Comedy boss cues and any character who is ridiculous and dangerous at once.

params.accent: 1 and 2 in a two beat feel, strong weak strong weak
params.bass: root and fifth alternating on the two beats
params.kit: backbeat snare on 2 and 4, driving eighths on the hat
params.harmony: i to V, or i to bVII to i
params.cell: two beats, repeated four times per 8 bar phrase

forbidden: swinging the eighths
a drum kit that follows the polka accent, which doubles the joke and kills it
more than two chords in the loop

recipes.name: Drum genre switch
recipes.when_to_use: Per location. The kit, not the harmony, tells the player what kind of scene this is.

params.boss_or_battle: four on the floor or rock backbeat, 16th hats, fill every 4 bars
params.town: half time, no kick on 1 and 3, soft decay noise
params.emotional: no kit, or one hit per phrase
params.dance: four on the floor, clap on 2 and 4, offbeat hats
params.kick_route: noise burst, or DPCM kick in battle cues
params.hat_route: noise with a 1 to 2 frame decay, periodic mode for metallic hits

forbidden: the same kit in a town and a boss cue
a fill landing a frame late
a drum machine pattern with no swing in a comedy cue

recipes.name: Triangle as a soundfont bass replacement
recipes.when_to_use: Every cue. Fox's bass comes from a soundfont, and the triangle is the nearest chip equivalent.

params.median_pitch: MIDI 36, two and a half octaves under the melody
params.note_length_median: 0.44 s, so re-attack rather than hold
params.articulation: 2 frame gap between notes, no sustain overlap
params.motion: approach notes into each chord change, one per change
params.chord_bass_melody_target: high, keep within 12 semitones of the melody's motion direction
params.vrc6_alternative: sawtooth octave down for weight, triangle kept for definition

forbidden: a held root for a whole bar
the bass doubling the melody in the same octave
sub bass below the triangle range

recipes.name: Harpsichord pluck for royalty
recipes.when_to_use: Castle, throne and royal court cues, where one instrument must signify rank.

params.decay: fast pluck, 4 to 6 frames to half volume, no sustain
params.role: countermelody or doubled descent, never the hook
params.documented_use: a harpsichord descent from bar 41 of a 144 bpm boss cue

forbidden: the harpsichord carrying the hook
arpeggiating the harpsichord part, which turns plucks into a buzz
using it in a town or field cue

recipes.name: One DPCM vocal event per cue
recipes.when_to_use: Character cues that need a voice where a choir is impossible.

params.sample_length: one word or one shout, under 0.5 s
params.placement: section boundary or the hook's second statement
params.pitch: fixed, or one repeat an octave down
params.documented_model: unintelligible vocals plus one audible phrase from an earlier track

forbidden: a sung line longer than two words
a DPCM voice under the hook
more than one vocal event in a loop

recipes.name: Loop seam by fragment, not by cadence
recipes.when_to_use: Every loop. The last bar must point at bar 1 without closing.

params.last_bar: state the cell's first 2 notes, or a fragment, and stop before resolution
params.cadence: avoid an authentic cadence in the last bar
params.bass: land on the dominant or on a note that steps into bar 1's root
params.drums: end the fill on the beat, not before it
params.check: play bars 15 to 16 then 1 to 2 and listen for a seam

forbidden: a tonic resolution in the final bar
a reversed fill
a full stop and restart

recipes.name: Three key areas in a boss track
recipes.when_to_use: A final boss cue of 2 minutes or more that must escalate without new cells.

params.key_plan: home key for 55 s, a bright key a minor third up or a major third away for 28 s, a darker key for 14 s, then return
params.documented_plan: B flat minor to C sharp major at 0:55, then E flat minor at 2:03, in a 2:22 track at 140 bpm
params.transition: one bar of the new key's dominant, or a chromatic bass walk
params.cells: same cells in all three areas

forbidden: more than three key areas
a key change under the hook's first statement
a key change with no bass preparation

recipes.name: Recognition budget guard
recipes.when_to_use: Every transformed statement, before delivery.

invariants: first interval sign and rough size
rhythm ratio first to last attack
register within 12 semitones of the original median
direction of the first three notes
params.contour_rule: contour carries recognition first, exact intervals later
params.tool: tools/melody_guard.py must pass, and the cell must be listed in the cue's motif spans

forbidden: changing three or more invariants in one statement
a transformed statement that the motif span record cannot identify
passing the guard by shortening the cell below 3 notes

recipes.name: Unison recitation surface
recipes.when_to_use: Battle and field cues where the rhythm, not the pitch, must carry the identity.

params.duration_surface: 0.60 of durations are a single sixteenth, 0.25 two sixteenths, 0.10 four
params.leap_target: at least one leap of a 5th or more per 4 bars

forbidden: a surface of held notes in a battle cue
unison share above 0.35, which stops being rhythmic and starts being a drone
all steps and no leaps

recipes.name: Late resolution on the hook peak
recipes.when_to_use: Every hook. The memorable note is the one that is not in the chord.

params.peak_note: a suspension, ninth or fourth over the chord, sounding on the strong beat
params.resolution: at the next bar, or on the weak half of the same bar
params.chord_melody_tension: aim high, the reference set runs 69 to 92 on a 50 average scale
params.harmony: keep the chord simple so the tension is audible, chord complexity 11 to 59

forbidden: resolving on the same beat the peak sounds
chord tone share above 0.75
adding harmonic complexity to create tension instead of a non-chord melody note

recipes.name: Inversion with rhythm and register held
recipes.when_to_use: A cue where a character's meaning turns: loyalty to threat, sun to defeat, tide to storm.

params.operation: negate every interval in semitones, keep the rhythm and the register band

forbidden: inverting the rhythm as well as the intervals
inverting and swapping the mode in the same statement
inverting a three note cell twice and calling the third statement a variation

recipes.name: Augmentation and diminution ladder
recipes.when_to_use: Memory cue, harmonic ground, or a rhythmic tag inside a battle loop.

params.tempo_compensation: to keep the same sounding length at half tempo, double the factor twice
params.bar_fit: factor 2 fills 1.5 bars of 4/4, factor 4 fills 3 bars

forbidden: augmenting and changing the mode in the same statement
factor 4 on a cell longer than 4 notes at battle tempo
diminution on a cell shorter than 3 attacks, which reads as a drum fill

recipes.name: Mode swap on the accompaniment only
recipes.when_to_use: The default way to recolour a cue when the cell must survive unchanged.

params.melody_rule: leave the cell's intervals untouched, the mode change happens in the chords
params.one_exception: one story moment may change the cell's vector, for example K from A minor to A major where minus 4 becomes minus 3
params.check: re-measure the interval vector after the swap, it must equal the original

forbidden: swapping the mode and inverting the intervals in the same statement
a swap that moves the first interval by two or more semitones without a story reason
changing mode twice inside one loop

recipes.name: Tempo multiplier ladder
recipes.when_to_use: Any cue that reuses a cell at a new speed, and every flashback, panic and machine cue.

params.arithmetic: at 124.5 bpm one beat is 0.482 s and a 3 beat cell is 1.45 s
params.documented_extremes: 15 percent speed on a whole track, and 92 percent playback in game

forbidden: a multiplier above 1.5 with reverb on the lead
changing tempo mid section without a drum fill or a bar of silence
0.5 on a cell that contains a dotted quarter and no augmentation

recipes.name: Rhythmic displacement set
recipes.when_to_use: Cheapest variation available: it costs no new material and changes at most one invariant.

params.shift_eighth: start the cell on the and of 1, the first leap lands on beat 2
params.shift_sixteenth: start on the e of 1, reads as an error until it repeats, then reads as style
params.rebar_3_4: keep the notes, give the dotted quarter a whole bar, the loop becomes 8 bars instead of 6
params.rotate: start from the third attack, a new cell related to the parent by fragment extraction
params.silence_subtraction: remove one attack, the cell becomes a call with a gap
params.invariant_cost: displacement alone changes at most one invariant

forbidden: displacing and transposing by more than a fifth in the same statement
a sixteenth shift that does not repeat within 4 bars
re-barring without recomputing the loop length in bars

recipes.name: Instrumentation swap with the two invariant rule
recipes.when_to_use: Reusing a cell in a new scene, where the arrangement should change before the melody does.

routes.pulse 0.125 fast decay: music box memory or a child scene
routes.vrc6 saw: pad or drone, never the lead
routes.vrc6 pulse 3: fragment quote, a fifth or an octave from the lead

params.documented_models: the same melody as solo guitar, then piano and strings, then music box; the same cell as orchestra, polka and harpsichord

forbidden: swapping the instrument and the mode in the same statement
a swap that changes only the pitch
the saw as the lead voice
